Dear Mara,

The office kept the window open even after the rain found the sill. I moved the papers to the dry end of the desk and left the wet ones where they were, because drying them would have made a worse mess. A bus stalled under the awning and the queue did not complain. They watched the water run off the roof in one steady line.

By noon the street had changed colour and the lamp in the window had come on by itself. I counted the gaps between the buses again and wrote the numbers in the margin, not the buses. The work was the gaps. The buses were only the thing that made a gap visible.

Yours,
Nia
